lines.line: node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints Hello, <name>! in upper case, for example HELLO, ADA!
lines.evidence: Tried: a build that ignores --shout (as bin/greet.js does today, since it skips args starting with '--'), a build that uppercases only the name ('Hello, ADA!'), and a build that hardcodes Ada. The run proof 'node bin/greet.js --shout Ada' catches the first two. The line's words cover any <name>, so a reader who tries a second name catches the hardcoded one. The obvious implementation, greeting(name).toUpperCase(), works whatever the argument order, because the existing parser finds the name wherever it sits.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
lines.evidence: Tried: a build that makes shouting the default, or one that breaks the name lookup when the flag is absent. Running 'node bin/greet.js Ada' must print 'Hello, Ada!', and the existing test/greet.test.js 'cli' test already asserts that exact output, so both are caught.

lines.line: docs/index.md documents the --shout option with an example
lines.evidence: The request asks for the docs 'next to the existing usage'. This line asks only that --shout be documented somewhere with an example. Wrong build: replace the current block in docs/index.md ('node bin/greet.js <name>' / 'Prints `Hello, <name>!`.') with only 'node bin/greet.js --shout Ada' → 'HELLO, ADA!'. Or keep the old block but give an example with the wrong output, such as 'Prints Hello, Ada!'. Either one meets the line: the option is documented and there is an example. But the first removes the existing usage it was meant to sit next to, and the second documents the wrong behavior. Missing: the line should say the existing usage stays, that --shout is documented next to it, and that the example shows the upper-case output (HELLO, ADA!).

lines.line: npm test passes and includes a test that runs node bin/greet.js --shout Ada and asserts it prints HELLO, ADA!
lines.evidence: Tried: a test that only checks src/greet.js, a test that asserts nothing, and a skipped test. The line requires a test that runs the CLI with --shout Ada and asserts the output, and 'npm test' (node --test) must pass locally. Reading the test catches all three. The existing 'cli' test guards the plain path. No CI is involved: pages.yml only publishes docs.

result.wrong_build: Strongest found: in bin/greet.js, detect --shout and print greeting(name).toUpperCase(). Add a test in test/greet.test.js that asserts execFileSync('node', ['bin/greet.js','--shout','Ada']) equals 'HELLO, ADA!\n'. In docs/index.md, replace the existing usage block with only 'node bin/greet.js --shout <name>' and an example. This meets all four lines, but it removes the documented plain usage instead of adding --shout next to it, which the request explicitly asked for. Line 3 is the nearest line and should require keeping the existing usage and placing a correct --shout example beside it.
